items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The owner manager was a Mr. Johhny Powell... We started working there on a percentage basis because Johnny Powell could not afford to pay a regular salary.

ctx.x: After one week of eating in this manner, Lloyd came around and told us that he had a job for us in a cabaret for the rest of the month in January. The name of the place was the Capitol at 140th Street and Lenox Avenue under a big Chinese restaurant. Lloyd had played in the Capitol with a famous orchestra. The owner manager was a Mr. Johhny Powell and the cabaret had been one of the most popular clubs in Harlem.

We started working there on a percentage basis because Johnny Powell could not afford to pay a regular salary. The Capitol had lost its popalaty and business was not good, but Johnny was trying to keep the place going in hope that it would become popular again. We had to play behind a couple of women singers who's names I don't remember. They went from table to table when ever there were enough people for them to sing to. I had not worked in a cabaret before and this was something new to me. If the singer recived…

Depending on how many people were in the place, a song could go on for as long as 45 minutes in which time we could each solo behind the singer 4 or 5 times. There was also the kitty which helped us also. The kitty was the box with a slot in the top and/whenever a person demanded the band to play a certain number and if we knew the number, they were obliged to put some money in the kitty which we did not have to divide with the singers.
